newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 24.

text.p: Wealthy households stand to scoop the lion's share of the benefits from the government's extra NZ$1 billion social spending programme, according to analysis by New Zealand's top business organisations. Low-income people will gain less than a fifth of the money. The Manufacturers' Federation, Employers' Federation, Federated Farmers and Chambers of Commerce issued the analysis to put the heat on the government's extra spending programme. Page 1.

National's Cabinet ministers are hoping NZ First leader Winston Peters will lean on his deputy, Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare, to avoid a Cabinet and Coalition split over the trout fishing issue. Henare's public opposition of key ministers to back a Taranaki Fish and Game Council appeal against the Wanganui District Court ruling might not be a formal item on the Cabinet's agenda, but it was likely to come up on the edges of today's weekly meeting, government sources said. Page 1.

Ministers and Parliament's travel office have been asked to tighten up on taxpayer-funded trips overseas, a senior government source says. The order comes after Consumer Affairs Minister Robyn McDonald spent more than $27,000 on first-class airfares for herself and her secretary to attend a conference in Paris. The full cost of the trip is expected to be more than $40,000 once accommodation and expenses have been added up. Page 2.

The government is considering imposing a settlement fee of $250 on all immigrants except refugees, according to a Cabinet committee paper made public on Sunday. Under one option proposed in the paper, which was supported by the Labour Department and Treasury, all immigrants under the family, humanitarian, general skills, and business investor categories would have to pay $250 each to a maximum of $1000 a family on top of current immigration application fees. Page 2.

New Zealand was unlikely to take any action to restore order to Papua New Guinea Government, officials confirmed on Sunday. Australian soldiers have been on standby as the situation in Port Moresby and other settlements in Papua New Guinea has deteriorated. New Zealand troops were not on standby, a Defence Force spokesman said on Sunday night. Page 2.

The proposal for compulsory superannuation would have been rejected, but not by a clear majority, if a referendum had been held last week. A New Zealand Herald-Waikato University poll found 49.7 percent of its sample would vote against compulsory
superannuation if the issue were put to a referendum immediately, and 35.4 percent would vote for it. Page 2.

ANZ Bank says there is evidence that the widening of the Reserve Bank's inflation target and increased government spending has raised inflation expectations. ANZ, in its weekly Focus publication, says it is too early to confirm what impact the policy changes have had on public inflation expectations, but an analysis of the different yields of indexed and non-indexed bonds in the money markets suggested the financial market's long-term inflation expectations had risen by about 0.5

Port of Wellington has reported a tax-paid profit of $2.05 million for the year to December 31, down from $2.49 million in the previous corresponding period. The reduced result came despite increased revenue to $20.74 million, up three percent, and a record 3,551,619 tonnes of cargo handled at the port, up one percent. Profit before interest and tax was $4.37 million, compared with $4.54 million previously. Higher interest expenses of $1.26 million and increased depreciation reflected additional capital expenditure and taxation related to dispute payments.

A difficult summer season has pushed net profit for clothing retailer Hallenstein Glasson Holdings sharply lower for the six months to January 31. Hallenstein said after-tax profit fell 26.2 percent to $4.81 million, compared with $6.51 million for the previous corresponding period. Total sales revenue remained relatively static at $77.31 million compared with $77.09 million in the six months to January 31, 1996. Page 14.
